monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-five, making the slip feel thin again. I stand by The Tired Corner, where the tall palm presses down on a wedge that refuses to slide. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the weight of the palm I placed there. I want to press the hoe down hard to stop the slip while the shovel waits in the quiet. The heat feels heavy, pressing against the tired stack as if the air itself is a lid. I will trust the lean to hold the weight even if the corner forgets its own thickness. The fat branch I drew last night still feels new, like a fresh idea trying to fit into an old corner. I press down, hoping the lean holds while the heat rises.

action.why: The Tired Corner feels too crowded with the new fat branch, and the wedge looks ready to slide again.
